correctness.rationale: For fixed a, let D be the edges with unequal diagonal labels, and B be those with equal labels and nonzero edge coefficient. In the centralizer equations each edge in D uniquely specifies its own off-diagonal unknown, while edges in B require equality of the diagonal unknowns on each component of (V,B). The other off-diagonal unknowns are free. This gives rank |D|+|V|−c(B) in every characteristic. Thus formal active-edge count overstates rank by one precisely when B contains the whole cycle. A separate expansion of the formal count writes the weight for a pair of diagonal colors as qz+(1−z) times the equality indicator added to qz, that is, qz+(1−z)·1_{equal}. Expanding over edge subsets F gives (qz)^(m−|F|)(1−z)^|F| q^{c(F)}. Using c(F)=m−|F| except for F containing the cycle (where it is one larger) gives U^m+(q−1)(1−z)^ℓ U^t. Exactly q(q−1)^ℓ cycle assignments need the rank correction, with independent tree factor U^t, proving the stated polynomial. Rank zero gives exactly the q scalar elements; dividing by q and extracting the linear coefficient yields the stated rank-one count because ℓ≥4. Summing q^{2m−rank} gives q^{2m}R(1/q) and simplifies to the commuting-pair formula. A separate exact check enumerated all pairs of eight-bit coefficient vectors for the four-cycle over F₂, testing the four edge commutator equalities modulo two; it yielded 10048 commuting pairs and rank counts (2,8,60,106,80). This checks one sample only; the all-field assertion is algebraic. The supplied modular-elimination script was inspected, not run.

evidence: The Oct. 12 catalogue entry's Finding, equation (1), sums over graphic-matroid flats Z with factor χ_{G/Z}(q) q^(m−|Z|), and over S⊆Z with weight (q−1)^|S| T^(m−|Z|+r_G(S)); it covers any simple graph and orientation. broader_coverage.reasoning: For fixed diagonal labels Z is their equality-edge set, and S is the set of equal-label edges with nonzero coefficients. In a unicycle r_G(S)=|S|−1 exactly when S contains the full cycle. Thus the general theorem specializes to the same count and the same exceptional correction, not just to a related finite-field distribution.

originality.rationale: This height-two incidence algebra is exactly the radical-square-zero quiver algebra of the bipartite orientation, with the same basis and products and hence the same adjoint ranks. A distinct general published catalogue result includes this all-rank enumerator; another states the identical closed unicyclic polynomial for arbitrary orientations and even allows odd cycles. The rank-one multiplicity and commuting-pair formula are immediate from that enumerator. This is mathematical coverage; catalogue path dates alone do not establish historical priority.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not decided by catalogue dates. An unlocated broader commuting-probability theorem for square-zero extensions and the unavailable primary Fortuin–Kasteleyn text leave some external comparison incomplete, but do not affect the exact catalogue match.
